newsitem.title: USA: U.S. "puzzled" over anti-West remarks by Lebed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. "puzzled" over anti-West remarks by Lebed.

text.p: The United States expressed puzzlement on Wednesday over harsh anti-Western and anti-Russian government remarks by Russia's national security chief Alexander Lebed and suggested they should be retracted.

Lebed, in an interview with the newspaper Vechernyaya Moskva, condemned U.S. missile attacks on Iraq this month and warned that if that happened to Russia: "I would hit back instantly. With everything we've got."
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the remarks were "quite puzzling to us. We feel our relationship with Russia is on a very good footing."

Burns told reporters some of the remarks clashed with views expressed by other Russian leaders such as President Boris Yeltsin, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov. He suggested that the remarks might "need some explanation and walking back."

In the interview, Lebed, a 46-year-old former general who is not a member of the government but is thought to have presidential ambitions, also said the Moscow government's failure to pay soldiers' wages could spark an armed mutiny.
But Burns said: "The United States has great confidence in the Russian government."

Lebed aides on Tuesday flatly denied he had given an interview to Britain's Daily Telegraph, which quoted him as saying Moscow would hit German and U.S. industrial interests if the NATO alliance admitted East European states.

But in the Russian newspaper interview published on Wednesday, Lebed promised to take a "tough line" with NATO officials in Brussels over the expansion issue when he visits alliance headquarters next month.
